cards.title: Business Problem
cards.subtitle: O2C Receivables Intelligence & DSO Steering
cards.description: The scenario describes a manufacturing business where receivables and order-book reporting are reviewed in separate extracts. DSO, overdue ageing and dispute exposure are calculated manually, while open orders, blocked orders, deliveries and financial receivables remain disconnected. This delays dispute discovery, makes credit intervention reactive and limits end-to-end cycle-time visibility.

cards.title: Five Key Business Questions
cards.subtitle: O2C Receivables Intelligence & DSO Steering
cards.description: What is my DSO trend by company code and customer group over the last 13 months, and which 10 customers move it most? What is my ageing waterfall today (current / 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / 90+), and how did it shift versus last month? Where is order-to-cash cycle time leaking — order-to-delivery, delivery-to-billing or billing-to-collection? Which customers exceed 80% of credit limit including open orders and deliveries, and what revenue is at risk if blocked? What cash can I realistically expect to collect in the next 30 days based on due dates and historical payment behaviour?

The page combines regional receivables concentration, DSO trend by company code, ageing distribution, top high-risk customers and geographic receivables/credit analysis. Lower panels highlight customers with the highest amount due and receivables risk concentration by region and customer group. Sldie 6 : Callouts Headline cards show Total Credit Limit (₹464.20 crore), Total Credit Exposure (₹296.24 crore), Credit Utilization (63.82%), Revenue at Risk (₹168.84 crore) and 4 blocked customers. The page compares credit exposure with credit limits, analyses product-division risk and surfaces product financial risk and customers requiring immediate credit-risk attention.
